items: Owner reported a live production smoke test of "Container Gardening for Beginners" stopped at 30% with 'We couldn't finish your ebook' and a 'Try again' button that did nothing -- an unacceptable dead end for a paid customer.

Read-only diagnosis first, before any code change: traced 30% to exactly 3 of 10 build stages validated (research, title, outline), with the manuscript stage ('Writing your chapters') stuck at FAILED_FINAL. Confirmed via code that completed stages were safely persisted (stage_is_validated reads the real rail, not a self-set flag).

Found two real, confirmed bugs: services/ebook_build_orchestrator.py never reset a stage's attempt counter once MAX_STAGE_ATTEMPTS was reached, so every future /advance call re-failed instantly without even attempting the stage; static/js/app.js's openEbookBuild() only called /advance when a build was not already failed, so 'Try again' only re-fetched read-only status and re-rendered the identical failure card, forever.

Verified the manuscript stage's existing resume-without-duplication design (services/ebook_project_workspace.py's idempotency-on-success-only key, accepted-chapter skip logic in services/ebook_manuscript_engine.py) was already sound and needed no changes -- it was simply unreachable.

Implemented the smallest safe fix: services.ebook_build_orchestrator.resume_build() clears only the one stalled stage's attempt count (never runs a stage, never touches a completed one) and a new POST /ebook/build/<id>/resume route; the ebook build screen's 'Try again' button is replaced everywhere with a working 'Resume Build' action, with plain-language wording and no technical detail.

Added tests/test_ebook_build_resume_recovery.py (17 tests, zero paid calls): reproduces the original bug, proves Resume Build clears the ceiling without ever calling a stage runner, proves Resume then the normal poll makes real progress, proves a transient failure still recovers automatically with no customer action, proves completed stages are never re-attempted, proves a normal successful build is unaffected, and proves 'Try again' no longer appears anywhere in the ebook build UI.
